items.title: Pullbacks of meromorphic functions are defined in seven situations ranging from flatness to weak association assumptions
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma lists seven geometric situations in which pullbacks of meromorphic functions along a morphism are defined, ranging from flat morphisms to hypotheses on where weakly associated or associated points are sent (statement lines 5983-6004). The counted proof is a clean reduction: it localizes to a ring map and, by the criterion for regular sections, reduces to showing that nonzerodivisors are preserved; it disposes of the flat case directly by injectivity of multiplication, proves the main case by observing that a nonzerodivisor avoids all minimal primes so that the hypothesis on weakly associated points makes its image a nonzerodivisor, and then specializes to the remaining cases using the comparison between associated and weakly associated primes and the description of weakly associated points of reduced schemes (proof lines 6006-6031). It is H2: every case is derived in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard prime-theoretic facts.
